front_blocks.md: Define **translator**.

back_blocks.md: A translator is a program that **translates program source code into machine code** so that it can be executed directly by a processor.

cards.front_md: Define **translator**.
cards.back_md: A translator is a program that **translates program source code into machine code** so that it can be executed directly by a processor.

front_blocks.md: Which type of translator is used for a low-level language such as assembly code?

back_blocks.md: An **assembler** translates low-level assembly code into machine code.

cards.front_md: Which type of translator is used for a low-level language such as assembly code?
cards.back_md: An **assembler** translates low-level assembly code into machine code.

front_blocks.md: An assembler translates <u>**                  **</u> written in assembly language into machine code.

back_blocks.md: An assembler translates **mnemonics** written in assembly language into machine code.

cards.back_md: An assembler translates **mnemonics** written in assembly language into machine code.

front_blocks.md: How much machine code does an assembler produce for each line of assembly language?

back_blocks.md: Each line of assembly language is assembled into **a single machine code instruction**.

cards.front_md: How much machine code does an assembler produce for each line of assembly language?
cards.back_md: Each line of assembly language is assembled into **a single machine code instruction**.

front_blocks.md: Define **compiler**.

back_blocks.md: A compiler translates a high-level language into machine code **all in one go**.

cards.front_md: Define **compiler**.
cards.back_md: A compiler translates a high-level language into machine code **all in one go**.

front_blocks.md: Define **interpreter**.

back_blocks.md: An interpreter translates a high-level language into machine code **one line at a time**.

cards.front_md: Define **interpreter**.
cards.back_md: An interpreter translates a high-level language into machine code **one line at a time**.

front_blocks.md: At which stage of development is a compiler normally used?

back_blocks.md: A compiler is generally used when a program **is finished** and has been checked for syntax errors.

cards.front_md: At which stage of development is a compiler normally used?
cards.back_md: A compiler is generally used when a program **is finished** and has been checked for syntax errors.

front_blocks.md: At which stage of development is an interpreter normally used?

back_blocks.md: An interpreter is generally used when a program **is being written**, in the development stage.

cards.front_md: At which stage of development is an interpreter normally used?
cards.back_md: An interpreter is generally used when a program **is being written**, in the development stage.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An interpreter generates machine code directly.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An interpreter does **not** generate machine code directly; appropriate **machine code subroutines** are called instead.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An interpreter generates machine code directly.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

An interpreter does **not** generate machine code directly; appropriate **machine code subroutines** are called instead.

front_blocks.md: What happens when an interpreter finds an error?

back_blocks.md: Each line is executed after translation, and if any errors are found the **process stops**.

cards.front_md: What happens when an interpreter finds an error?
cards.back_md: Each line is executed after translation, and if any errors are found the **process stops**.

front_blocks.md: Give one disadvantage of using an assembler.

back_blocks.md: Assembly code is **difficult to write** because the commands are limited and hard to understand, any change means it **must be reassembled**, and it is **designed solely for one specific processor**.

cards.front_md: Give one disadvantage of using an assembler.
cards.back_md: Assembly code is **difficult to write** because the commands are limited and hard to understand, any change means it **must be reassembled**, and it is **designed solely for one specific processor**.

front_blocks.md: Which runs faster, a compiled program or an interpreted program?

back_blocks.md: A **compiled** program runs faster, because translation is done in advance and **optimised machine code** is used.

cards.front_md: Which runs faster, a compiled program or an interpreted program?
cards.back_md: A **compiled** program runs faster, because translation is done in advance and **optimised machine code** is used.

front_blocks.md: What software does an end user need to run a compiled program?

back_blocks.md: An end user needs only the **executable file**, not the compiler, so there is no extra cost or setup.

cards.front_md: What software does an end user need to run a compiled program?
cards.back_md: An end user needs only the **executable file**, not the compiler, so there is no extra cost or setup.

front_blocks.md: Why can a user not modify a compiled program?

back_blocks.md: Users **do not receive the source code**, so they cannot modify or extend the program.

cards.front_md: Why can a user not modify a compiled program?
cards.back_md: Users **do not receive the source code**, so they cannot modify or extend the program.

front_blocks.md: Interpreted programs must be interpreted on the same type of machine, so they are less <u>**                **</u>.

back_blocks.md: Interpreted programs must be interpreted on the same type of machine, so they are less **portable**.

cards.front_md: Interpreted programs must be interpreted on the same type of machine, so they are less <u>**                **</u>.
cards.back_md: Interpreted programs must be interpreted on the same type of machine, so they are less **portable**.

front_blocks.md: Why is an interpreter easier to debug with than a compiler?

back_blocks.md: Errors are **caught one line at a time** and the developer can **view partial results as they go**, making it easier to test and refine the program.

cards.front_md: Why is an interpreter easier to debug with than a compiler?
cards.back_md: Errors are **caught one line at a time** and the developer can **view partial results as they go**, making it easier to test and refine the program.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A compiled program will still run if it contains syntax errors.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Why is it harder for a developer to monetise an interpreted program?

back_blocks.md: The developer **loses control over the code**, which makes it harder to **charge for upgrades** or prevent copying.

cards.front_md: Why is it harder for a developer to monetise an interpreted program?
cards.back_md: The developer **loses control over the code**, which makes it harder to **charge for upgrades** or prevent copying.

front_blocks.md: Define **mixed mode translation**.

back_blocks.md: Mixed mode translation **combines features of both a compiler and an interpreter**, compiling the program into an **intermediate form** that is then **interpreted at runtime**.

cards.front_md: Define **mixed mode translation**.
cards.back_md: Mixed mode translation **combines features of both a compiler and an interpreter**, compiling the program into an **intermediate form** that is then **interpreted at runtime**.

front_blocks.md: What is source code compiled into in mixed mode translation?

back_blocks.md: The source code is compiled into **intermediate code**, such as **bytecode**, rather than full machine code.

cards.front_md: What is source code compiled into in mixed mode translation?
cards.back_md: The source code is compiled into **intermediate code**, such as **bytecode**, rather than full machine code.

front_blocks.md: What interprets the intermediate code in mixed mode translation?

back_blocks.md: The intermediate code is interpreted by a **virtual machine**, for example the **Java Virtual Machine (JVM)**.

cards.front_md: What interprets the intermediate code in mixed mode translation?
cards.back_md: The intermediate code is interpreted by a **virtual machine**, for example the **Java Virtual Machine (JVM)**.

front_blocks.md: What does just-in-time (JIT) compilation do?

back_blocks.md: Just-in-time compilation converts some parts of the intermediate code **into machine code at runtime**, which improves performance.

cards.front_md: What does just-in-time (JIT) compilation do?
cards.back_md: Just-in-time compilation converts some parts of the intermediate code **into machine code at runtime**, which improves performance.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A mixed mode program executes faster than a fully compiled program.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **fully compiled** program is fastest. Mixed mode translation gives **medium** speed, although JIT compilation makes it faster over time.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A mixed mode program executes faster than a fully compiled program.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A **fully compiled** program is fastest. Mixed mode translation gives **medium** speed, although JIT compilation makes it faster over time.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of mixed mode translation over a compiler.

back_blocks.md: Mixed mode translation is **highly portable across platforms**, whereas fully compiled code is **not portable**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of mixed mode translation over a compiler.
cards.back_md: Mixed mode translation is **highly portable across platforms**, whereas fully compiled code is **not portable**.

cards.front_md: What does syntax highlighting do?

front_blocks.md: How does syntax highlighting help a programmer?

back_blocks.md: It helps programmers **quickly identify and differentiate code components**, which reduces the chance of syntax errors and improves code comprehension.
